qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Duopoly with Western Digital in high-capacity 3.5" HDDs backed by proprietary Heat-Assisted Magnetic Recording (HAMR/Mozaic) head and media technology. However, moat fails the economic test: 10-year median ROIC of 11.2% falls short of the 12% threshold, gross margins swing wildly from 18% in troughs to 45%+ at cyclical peaks, and structural $/TB storage deflation combined with concentrated hyperscaler purchasing power prevents consistent inflation-plus pricing.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Pricing & Proof of Moat, REJECT). While Seagate and Western Digital form a tight duopoly in mass-capacity HDDs with proprietary HAMR/Mozaic engineering know-how (Gate 3a), the business suffers from severe cyclical earnings volatility, structural $/TB price deflation, and extreme customer concentration among cloud hyperscalers who extract price concessions. 10-year median ROIC is 11.2%, failing the 12% hurdle. In downcycles, operating margins swing negative and equity was wiped into negative territory (-$1.5B in FY2024), demonstrating an absence of inflation-plus pricing power.
qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle financial track record shows extreme cyclicality and sub-hurdle capital efficiency. 10-year median ROIC is 11.2% (below the 12% Munger threshold). In the FY2022–FY2024 downcycle, revenues fell ~44%, gross margin plunged to 18.3% in FY2023, operating margin turned negative, and net loss reached -$529M, pushing stockholders' equity to -$1.5B in FY2024 with ~$5.4B in debt. While AI mass-storage demand and tight supply discipline generated a strong cyclical rebound in FY2025–FY2026, storage hardware faces permanent price-per-terabyte deflation and monopsonistic pressure from cloud hyperscalers (Microsoft, AWS, Google, Meta). Long-term substitution risk from declining QLC NAND flash costs further limits durable pricing power.
